title: agentilda configuration
description: What a machine should have: which coding agents, which other executables, and which skills and plugins to give them. Read by scripts/install-sources from configuration.yml.

agents.description: The coding agents themselves. Also the set a source's `agents:` is matched against.

executables.description: Everything else this machine should have on PATH: the binaries a source's `install:` may call, and anything else worth having. Installed after `agents:` and before any source. Unlike `agents:`, these names are matched against nothing.

sources.description: Where skills and plugin bundles come from.

name.description: Installs as skills/<name> or plugins/<name>, so it may not contain a slash or whitespace.

regexp.description: A regular expression, optionally slashed: /re/, /re/i, or a bare re. Matched against the name a thing installs as, never its path inside the source.

name.description: How the run names it, and, when `exists:` is absent, the executable looked up on PATH to decide whether it is installed.

installer.description: The vendor's own install line. Runs through a shell, unlike a source's `install:`. Skipped when the entry is already present, unless -f is passed.

exists.description: How to tell whether this is already installed. Any command line, run through a shell, exit 0 meaning yes. Absent means: is something named `name` on PATH?

update.description: How to bring this up to date once it is installed, in the vendor's own terms. Any command line, run through a shell. Run only by `<block> update [name...]`, never by a routine sync, and never for an entry that is not installed.

tool.description: One entry under `agents:` or `executables:`. Both blocks have the same shape; they differ only in what the names are used for.

source.description: One entry under `sources:`. The type decides how it is fetched; everything else narrows what it contributes.

type.description: skills: every SKILL.md-rooted directory under `path` becomes its own skill. plugin: `path` is one bundle. plugins: every directory under `path` is a bundle of its own. command: no repository, `install:` is run instead.

path.description: The directory inside the source to install from. Defaults to the repository root, or to whichever of .claude/ or .agents/ a command wrote to.

adopt.description: Which halves a source contributes. Both by default.

include_skills.description: Install only what matches. May be paired with exclude_skills, in which case both apply in the order this file writes them and the last to match a name decides.

exclude_skills.description: Install everything except what matches. May be paired with include_skills, in which case both apply in the order this file writes them and the last to match a name decides.

include_plugins.description: Install only what matches. May be paired with exclude_plugins, in which case both apply in the order this file writes them and the last to match a name decides.

exclude_plugins.description: Install everything except what matches. May be paired with include_plugins, in which case both apply in the order this file writes them and the last to match a name decides.

agents.description: Which coding agents this source is for. Absent means portable, which is what most sources are.

oneAgentList.description: A source that both names and denies agents is a question with no defensible answer, so it is refused rather than resolved. The regular-expression pairs are not like this: both may be set, and they apply in the order the file writes them.

fetchedOneWay.description: A source is cloned or it runs a command, never both. Each branch declares the key it permits, so the matching branch evaluates it and the source's unevaluatedProperties rejects the other. No `not` clause is needed: naming `install:` on a source that clones leaves it unevaluated, which is already the error.

install.description: Split into words and run directly, never through a shell, with its working directory inside .sources/<name>.

pluginFiltersNeedBundles.description: include_plugins/exclude_plugins mean nothing on a type: skills source, which installs no bundles.
